text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--The Social Democrat-led minority coalition and left-wing opposition parties are working on a five billion crown economic package comprising cuts in tax exemption and new taxes on motorists and domestic air travel, with the better-off taking the brunt. The government, the Socialist People's Party and Unity List are expected to complete their negotiations early in the week.
--SAS (Scandinavian Airlines System) is believed to be planning new mass staff cuts of around 20,000 to be announced at a meeting between management and unions next week.

--FLS Industries is named share of the month after the cement, engineering and aerespace company posted eight percent higher turnover last year and a 68 percent better pre-tax profit and its troubled British-based FLS Aerospace unit won new orders, raising hopes of recovery.

--Mergers and takeovers are expected to dominate the booming Danish windmill and wind turbine industry within a few years. The windmill industry has grown into an international multi-billion crown market for what was recently only a niche industry in Denmark - Denmark is a leading player with six out of 10 windmills in the world Danish-manufactured.

--Four out of every five crowns profit in the Danish banking industry goes to beefing up banks' own capital but experts warn that the sector's general policy of not increasing dividends to shareholders cannot continue if banks post another good year in 1997.

--Danish biotechological group Novo Nordisk sells its insulin products in Denmark at prices 30-60 percent higher than in other European Union states. This costs the Danish taxpayer an estimated 40-90 million crowns a year and only a liberalisation of the industry can bring down insulin prices but deregulation seems still to be far off.
